newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: KL INTERBANK RATES STEADY IN THIN TRADING.
newsitem.headline: KL INTERBANK RATES STEADY IN THIN TRADING.

text.p: Malaysian interbank rates were mostly unchanged on Thursday morning in very thin trading with the market awaiting fresh lending by the central Bank Negara Malaysia, dealers said.
"There's no sign of agent banks' presence yet this morning," said a dealer with a Malaysian bank.
Agent banks of Bank Negara were last seen lending one-month money on Wednesday morning.
At 0200 GMT, the one-week money was steady at 6.2/4 percent.
One-month money at 7.25 percent and three-month at 7.4/5 percent, were also unchanged.
The overnight rate, which closed at 5.5/7 percent on Wednesday, was expected to remain below six percent, dealers said.
Dealers said the market was getting tight again as funds which banks borrowed from the central bank in July were starting to mature and leave the system.

Bank Negara has been lending funds, mostly one-month money, over the past month to help ease market tightness and bring interbank rates down, dealers said. Massive intervention by the central bank in the foreign exchange market in June to defend the ringgit from speculative attack had earlier caused a liquidity squeeze in the money market.
"I think Negara is injecting the funds back into the market," said another dealer.
